subject: HaloHealth: Priority throughput & 5xx stabilization — Command cadre update
messages:
From: Sara Liao <sara.liao@halohealth.com>
To: david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 22:12:00 -0800
Subject: Latency spikes + increase in 5xx on /v1/generate

David —

We saw a sharp latency spike and a 10x jump in 5xx errors starting ~17:40 UTC today on our production routing to your hosted endpoint (region: us-west). Impact: our clinical triage workflows are queueing; throughput fell from ~850 TPS to ~120 TPS and error rates are at ~6%.

What we observed:
- Higher tail latency on long-context requests (seq ~2048)
- Elevated GRPC 503 / internal errors, intermittent timeouts
- Dashboard attached (latency-dashboard-20261104.png) and a small error sample (error-sample-5xx.txt)

This is impacting patient-facing workflows. We need an exec-level readout and a concrete stabilization plan within 2 hours. Please advise immediate mitigation steps and when we can expect a normal service level.

Attached: latency-dashboard-20261104.png, error-sample-5xx.txt

—Sara
VP, Platform Engineering
HaloHealth
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Liao <sara.liao@halohealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 22:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Latency spikes + increase in 5xx on /v1/generate

Sara — thanks for the quick heads-up and the attachments. I understand the severity and have opened a command cadre. Immediate actions we are taking:

1) Routing: enabling regional failover to dedicated reserved pool for your workload (will start in next 3–5 mins).
2) Autoscale: pushing a temporary aggressive scale policy for your model variant.
3) Telemetry: collecting KV-cache + per-shard tail traces and aggregated gRPC error traces.
4) Smoke: running a synthetic runbook for long-context requests to validate recovery.

We will host an exec bridge at 23:00 PST — Zoom link to follow. I am CC'ing karthik (infra lead), Marissa (Customer Success), and Grace (product) to coordinate comms and remediation.

Expect a short status update in ~15 mins.

—David
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: david_kim@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 22:34:00 -08:00
Subject: ACTION: infra steps for HaloHealth surge & 5xx runbook

Team — quick ops notes from initial triage (raw):
- Observed per-GPU queue pileups on shards 2/5 for model: redwood-llama-70b-ctx. Long-context traffic is increasing KV reads and causing higher memory pressure.
- gRPC 503s correlate with a spike in context-eviction errors; not a network-wide route flapping.

Immediate checklist (I will run these):
- [x] Increase reserved capacity pool for HaloHealth to +40% (applied 22:28 PST).
- [ ] Enable prefix KV caching for repeated prompts (config toggle staged).
- [ ] Roll model variant to a quantized fallback that has lower mem footprint for seq>1024 (canarying to 3% of traffic).
- [ ] Collect and push /var/log/gpu/* and inference logs to the incident bundle (server-logs-20261104.tar.gz).

If canary shows improvement on tail latency for long-context requests we will widen rollout. I need tokenized sample traces; Marissa can coordinate capture with Halo.

—Karthik
Director, Serving Infrastructure
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Liao <sara.liao@halohealth.com>, Eric Morales <em@halohealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 00:02:00 -08:00
Subject: HaloHealth incident update — 00:02 PST status & exec bridge 00:30 PST

Sara / Eric —

Quick status: we implemented the temporary reserved capacity increase and staged a canary roll to a quantized variant for long-context requests. Early indicators: tail p95 latency reduced ~38% on canary, 5xxs on canary are near 0.5%. Wide rollback is not required so far.

Planned next steps before wider rollout:
- Monitor canary for 30 mins for regression across throughputs (we're at ~40% of normal peak now).
- If green, widen to 50% traffic and enable prefix caching toggle for repeated clinical prompts.
- Prepare a postmortem and a longer-term recommendation (model compilation + kernel update) if results are transient.

Please join our exec bridge at 00:30 PST for an aligned readout — Zoom: https://zoom.us/j/999888777
Incident console: https://redwood.console/teams/halohealth/incidents/8421
Attached: redwood-playbook-surge.pdf, server-logs-20261104.tar.gz

—David

(Internal note: Marissa please lead the customer comms on the bridge, Jonas and Grace prepare slide 1: current metrics + next-step thresholds.)
From: Sara Liao <sara.liao@halohealth.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Eric Morales <em@halohealth.com>, procurement@halohealth.com
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 00:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: HaloHealth incident update — 00:02 PST status & exec bridge 00:30 PST

Thanks — appreciate the quick action and the canary results. We'll be on the bridge. I attached a small request: please preserve the raw error traces for the window 17:30–18:15 UTC for our internal audit. Also sharing a short sample of user request payloads that triggered the 5xxs (attached).

Forwarded message (error sample):

—Sara
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Liao <sara.liao@halohealth.com>, Eric Morales <em@halohealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -08:00
Subject: HaloHealth — post-bridge status & next steps (stabilized, but rolling checks)

Sara / Eric —

Post-bridge brief: canary widened to 60% at 01:10 PST and we observed sustained recovery — throughput is back to ~920 TPS (pre-incident baseline ~950 TPS) and 5xx rate is under 0.7% across traffic. We are not seeing memory-pressure re-emergence on the widened rollout.

Immediate next steps:
- We will keep the reserved capacity uplift for 24h and monitor autoscale metrics.
- Karthik's team will ship a kernel tuning patch in the next 72h and schedule a quiet-window deploy.
- Marissa will follow up with a customer-facing incident timeline and a draft SLA credit for the impacted window.

Closing notes: we preserved the raw traces and included them in the incident bundle. If you need a deeper telemetry export for your compliance team, we can run that on request.

Attachments included in the incident bundle: server-logs-20261104.tar.gz, latency-dashboard-20261104.png

Thanks for the partnership and patience — we'll keep monitoring and will share the postmortem within 5 business days.

—David
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
